q: 设计 Instagram 时，三条核心功能需求是？
q_en: When designing Instagram, what are the three core functional requirements?
options: 发布带照片/视频和说明的帖子；关注其他用户；按时间倒序查看所关注用户的 feed

发帖；关注用户；查看按机器学习模型排序的个性化 feed

Create posts with likes and comments; support searching users, hashtags, and locations.
Follow users; publish ephemeral Stories; enable real-time live streaming.
Create posts; follow users; view a feed personalized by a machine-learning ranking model.
why: 核心三条：发帖、关注、看时间序 feed。点赞评论、搜索、Stories、直播、算法排序都被划到范围外。

q: 在 CAP 权衡上应该怎么选？
q_en: For the CAP trade-off, which side should this Instagram feed design favor?
options: 强一致优先：所有新帖必须瞬间在全球所有副本上同时可见
可用性与强一致必须同时完全满足，两者缺一不可
可用性优先，接受最终一致（新帖最迟约 2 分钟对粉丝可见）
只对视频保证强一致，照片允许任意延迟，不做承诺
options_en: Prioritize strong consistency: every new post must be instantly visible on all global replicas.

Prioritize availability, accepting eventual consistency with posts visible within about two minutes.

why_en: This system prioritizes availability over consistency, accepting eventual consistency with posts visible to followers within about two minutes.

tradeoff: 可用性 + 最终一致 vs 强一致 + 全网瞬时可见

q: 补全 Instagram 的非功能需求：
q_en: Complete Instagram's core non-functional requirements.
text: 系统{{可用性}}优先于一致性（最终一致，窗口最多 {{2 分钟}}）；feed 请求端到端 < {{500ms}}；媒体要即时渲染；规模支撑 {{5亿}} DAU。

About one hundred gigabytes.

why: 100M × 1KB = 100GB/天，比媒体小三个数量级。若 DynamoDB 成本吃紧，不常访问的元数据同样可以下移到 S3。
why_en: One hundred million posts at one kilobyte of metadata each is about one hundred gigabytes of new metadata per day.

scenario: 10 年 750PB 的 S3 账单太贵，而其中大量老媒体几乎无人访问。
scenario_en: Ten years of 750PB in S3 is expensive, and much of the old media is rarely accessed.
q: 省钱的正确姿势是？
q_en: What is the right cost-saving storage strategy?
options: 把长期没人访问的老媒体定期直接永久删除
把所有的媒体数据不加区分地统一搬进 Redis 缓存
把老媒体打成 zip 压缩包但仍留在原来的存储层
把长期未访问的媒体下移到更冷存储层（如 Glacier），冷元数据同理下移
options_en: Periodically and permanently delete old media that nobody has accessed in a long time.
Move all media data indiscriminately into the Redis cache.
Zip up the old media into an archive but leave it in the original storage tier.
Move long-untouched media down to a colder tier like Glacier, and shift cold metadata down the same way.
why: 冷热分层是通用省钱模式：访问越少的数据放越冷（越便宜）的层。媒体去 Glacier、冷元数据去 S3，热数据留在原地。
why_en: Move media that has not been accessed in a long time to colder cheaper storage like Glacier, and likewise shift cold metadata out of DynamoDB.
whenOtherWins: 如果老内容仍被频繁回看（周年回顾、经典帖回流），Glacier 的取回延迟和费用反而伤体验，应留在标准层。
tradeoff: 冷热分层省成本 vs 统一标准层保低延迟
optionMeanings: 永久移除数据，用户以后再也无法访问这些历史内容。
把持久化对象存储的数据搬进易失性的内存缓存。
压缩后仍留在原来昂贵的存储层，没有降低成本。
按访问频率把冷数据下沉到更便宜的存储层，热数据留在原地。
optionScenarioImpacts: 用户会永久失去访问自己历史帖子的能力，产品体验受损。
Redis 内存成本远高于对象存储，且重启可能丢数据。
存储账单几乎不变，压缩带来的节省有限。
长期不访问的数据成本大幅下降，访问频繁的数据延迟不受影响。
optionDirectness: 删除数据违背了保留用户内容的产品预期。
用错了存储介质，成本方向反了。
没有解决核心的存储层级问题。
这是解决海量冷数据成本问题的标准做法。

Moves data from durable object storage into a volatile memory cache.
Stays compressed in the same expensive tier, barely saving anything.
Tiers cold data down to cheaper storage by access frequency, keeping hot data in place.

Redis memory costs far exceed object storage, and restarts can lose data.

Cold data cost drops sharply while frequently accessed data stays fast.

wrong storage medium, reverses the cost direction.

q: 补全存储温度层级（由热到冷）：
q_en: Complete the storage temperature hierarchy from hot to cold.
text: 存储由热到冷、由贵到省：{{CDN}} → 缓存/内存 → {{SSD}} → {{HDD}} → {{磁带}}；不常被访问的数据往下移一层就能省钱。
why: 「越热越贵」是存储的普适规律。任何成本讨论都可以落到这条链上：找出访问频率低的数据，把它往下挪。
why_en: Storage runs hot to cold from CDN to memory to SSD to HDD to tape, and rarely accessed data can always move down a level to save money.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["CDN(最热最贵)"] --> B["缓存/内存"]
    B --> C["SSD"]
    C --> D["HDD"]
    D --> E["磁带(最冷最省)"]

q: 微服务层面的吞吐扩展怎么做？
q_en: How should stateless microservices scale throughput?
options: 靠人工全天候盯着监控面板去手动添加机器
只做垂直扩展，一路不断买更大规格的单台机器
按 CPU/内存阈值自动水平扩缩容，每组服务前隐含负载均衡器分发流量
部署一台超大规格的单体 Redis 扛下全部业务流量
options_en: Have someone watch the dashboard around the clock to manually add machines.
Only scale vertically, continuously buying an ever-bigger single machine.
Auto-scale horizontally on CPU or memory thresholds, with a load balancer implicitly distributing traffic to each group.
Deploy one oversized monolithic Redis instance to absorb all business traffic.
why: 无状态微服务的标准打法：基于 CPU/内存指标自动水平扩缩，流量由每组服务前的负载均衡器分发。
why_en: Microservices scale horizontally and automatically based on CPU or memory thresholds, with an implicit load balancer in front of each scaled group.
diagram:
graph LR
    LB[Load balancer] --> Post[Post Service pool]
    LB --> Feed[Feed Service pool]
    LB --> Follow[Follow Service pool]
    Post --> DB1[(Post DB shards)]
    Feed --> Redis[(Feed cache shards)]
optionMeanings: 依赖人工判断和手动操作来响应流量变化。
把单机配置堆到硬件能买到的极限。
基于监控指标自动增减实例，负载均衡器分发流量。
让单个内存实例承担全部流量而不做分布式扩展。
optionScenarioImpacts: 响应速度慢，流量突增时容易来不及扩容。
扩容很快撞到单机硬件上限，且成本效率低。
流量增长时实例自动跟上，流量下降时自动收缩省钱。
单点故障和容量上限会让系统在高峰期直接崩溃。
optionDirectness: 效率低且响应慢，不是标准做法。
垂直扩展终会撞到硬件上限。
这是无状态微服务的行业标准做法。
不满足分布式、高可用的基本要求。
optionMeanings_en: Relies on manual judgment and action to react to traffic changes.
Pushes a single machine's spec to the hardware ceiling.
Auto-adjusts instance count on metrics, with a load balancer distributing traffic.
Puts all traffic on one memory instance with no distributed scaling.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Slow to react; traffic spikes can outrun manual scaling.
Scaling soon hits a hardware ceiling with poor cost efficiency.
Instances grow with traffic and shrink back down to save cost.
A single point of failure and capacity limit crashes under peak load.
optionDirectness_en: inefficient and slow, not the standard approach.
vertical scaling eventually hits a hardware ceiling.
the industry standard for stateless microservices.
fails basic distributed, high-availability requirements.

scenario: 面试官在 Instagram 系统设计面试里，对中级（mid-level）和高级（senior）候选人打分标准不同，主要看候选人在 feed 生成和媒体分发这两个深挖点上的表现。
scenario_en: In an Instagram system design interview, mid-level and senior candidates are judged differently, especially on feed generation and media delivery deep dives.
q: 中级和高级候选人的期望差异体现在哪？
q_en: How do expectations differ between mid-level and senior candidates?
options: 中级：给出可用高层设计，提示下能演进方案；高级：主动讲清 fan-out 权衡与选型论证
中级候选人必须在面试现场手写出可直接上线部署的生产级完整代码
系统设计面试对中级和高级候选人的期望标准完全一样，毫无区别
高级候选人完全不需要理解 feed 生成这个环节，只关注别的模块
options_en: Mid-level: a workable high-level design that evolves with hints; senior: independently explains fan-out trade-offs with justified choices.
Mid-level candidates must handwrite complete, deployable, production-ready code live in the interview.
The system design interview holds mid-level and senior candidates to exactly the same bar, with no distinction at all.
Senior candidates don't need to understand feed generation at all; only other modules matter to their evaluation.
why: 分水岭在「要不要提示」和深度：中级借提示改进即可；高级要自己驾驭 fan-out 权衡、名人混合方案、媒体上传与索引策略。
why_en: Mid-level candidates may need hints to evolve past fan-out on read, while seniors must independently master the fan-out trade-offs, the celebrity problem, and media handling.
optionMeanings: 准确刻画了两个级别在「是否需要提示」和「深度」上的差异。
混淆了系统设计面试和手写代码面试这两种不同的考察形式。
忽视了面试官对不同级别设定的真实差异化标准。
与实际情况相反，feed 生成恰恰是这道题的核心深挖点。
optionScenarioImpacts: 帮助候选人明确不同级别该展示到什么深度。
会让中级候选人误以为要当场手写可运行的生产代码。
会让候选人无法针对自己的级别调整表现策略。
会让高级候选人在最关键的深挖环节掉链子。
optionDirectness: 中级可以在提示下补方案，高级需要主动展开权衡。
只有代码轮才会要求可运行实现，系统设计轮看架构判断。
同一道题会按级别调深度，高级要少依赖提示。
feed 生成是核心深挖点，高级候选人必须能讲清。
optionMeanings_en: Accurately captures the gap in hint-dependence and depth between levels.
Conflates system design interviews with a separate hands-on coding interview.
Ignores that interviewers genuinely apply different bars per level.
Contradicts reality; feed generation is exactly the core deep-dive here.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Helps candidates calibrate the depth expected at their level.
Misleads mid-level candidates into thinking they must write runnable production code.
Leaves candidates unable to tailor their performance to their level.
Would trip up senior candidates at the exact deep-dive that matters most.
optionDirectness_en: Mid-level candidates may evolve with hints; seniors should lead the trade-off discussion.
Runnable implementation belongs in a coding round; this round evaluates design judgment.
The same prompt is calibrated by level, with seniors needing fewer hints.
Feed generation is a core deep dive, so senior candidates must explain it clearly.

scenario: 面试官对 Staff+ 候选人的评估重点，不是知识覆盖面，而是工程判断力：能不能在有限时间里抓住这道题真正的瓶颈。
scenario_en: For Staff+ candidates, the interviewer is testing engineering judgment, not breadth of memorized facts: can they find the real bottleneck under time pressure?
q: Staff+ 候选人在这道题上被考察什么？
q_en: What is a Staff+ candidate being evaluated on in this Instagram design question?
options: 要求候选人把所有 AWS 服务的具体名字都背得滚瓜烂熟
一开始就直接跳到设计最复杂、最重的分布式系统架构
只需要在白板上画出几个高层级的框图就已经足够了
快速锁定真正瓶颈、讲清规模演化路径、知道何时该升级，并预判故障与运维问题
options_en: Requiring the candidate to have every single AWS service name memorized cold.
Jumping straight into designing the heaviest, most complex distributed architecture from minute one.
Sketching just a few high-level boxes on the whiteboard is already enough.
Quickly locate the real bottlenecks, narrate the scale-evolution path, know when to upgrade, and anticipate failure and ops issues.
why: Staff 的信号是判断力：识别真瓶颈、按规模演化设计、复杂度只花在刀刃上，同时预判故障与运维成本。过早堆复杂度反而是减分项。
why_en: Staff candidates must quickly identify the real bottlenecks, articulate how the design evolves from one million to five hundred million users, and know when simpler solutions suffice.
optionMeanings: 考察的是知识记忆量，不是工程判断力。
一开始就堆最大复杂度，是常见的反模式。
只有框图缺少支撑细节，展现不出判断力的深度。
综合考察瓶颈识别、演化路径、复杂度取舍、故障预判四项判断力。
optionScenarioImpacts: 选它会让候选人误以为背知识点就能拿到 Staff 评价。
选它会让候选人从一开始就过度设计，反而暴露判断力不足。
选它会让候选人的设计缺少足够深度支撑评估。
准确展现候选人识别真正瓶颈、控制复杂度的能力。
optionDirectness: 背服务名只展示记忆，不展示如何取舍。
只有规模已经逼近瓶颈时，重架构才值得引入。
高层框图要配瓶颈、容量和故障分析才够 Staff 深度。
Staff 信号来自先找瓶颈，再按规模逐步升级设计。
optionMeanings_en: Tests rote knowledge, not engineering judgment.
Maxing out complexity from the start is a common anti-pattern.
Boxes alone without supporting detail don't show judgment depth.
Jointly tests bottleneck-spotting, evolution narrative, complexity trade-offs, and failure anticipation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Misleads candidates into thinking memorized facts earn a Staff rating.
Leads candidates to over-engineer from the start, exposing weak judgment.
Leaves the design too shallow to demonstrate real judgment.
Accurately shows the candidate's ability to spot bottlenecks and control complexity.
optionDirectness_en: Memorizing service names shows recall, not trade-off judgment.
Heavy architecture is justified only once scale creates the bottleneck.
High-level boxes need bottleneck, capacity, and failure analysis to feel Staff-level.
The Staff signal is finding bottlenecks first, then evolving the design with scale.
